findings.title: Guidance table breaks on rendering: pipe characters inside quotes Q-1..Q-4 truncate the quotes and drop the code-value column
findings.detail: The texts of quotes Q-1 to Q-4 in narrative.json are copied from the release's flattened table and contain the separator ' | | ' (e.g. Q-2 'Approximately 85.95% | | Approximately 86.25%'). note.md puts these quotes inside a three-column Markdown table, so each rendered row (computed/note_rendered.md lines 32-35) contains five cells instead of three. A GFM renderer ignores the extra cells, so the published table shows only the GAAP half of each quote with an unclosed quotation mark ('“Approximately 85.95%'), an empty cell, and no 'Code value used' column at all. As a result the non-GAAP guidance wording and all of the code-generated guidance figures ($61.5bn midpoint, 86.0% / 86.2%, $2.3bn / $2.1bn, $37.84 / $38.15) disappear from the table. The quotes are then shown truncated in a way the source does not support, and the evidence trail from quote to code value is broken. A related issue appears in Key points: Q-1 and Q-4 render as '$61.5 billion ± $1.5 billion | | $61.5 billion ± $1.5 billion' with no GAAP/non-GAAP labels. The underlying values themselves are correct; I checked them against release lines 161-178.
findings.required_evidence: Every rendered guidance-table row in note_rendered.md has exactly three cells, and each quote appears whole. One fix: give gen-narrative separate verbatim quotes without pipes for GAAP and non-GAAP (e.g. '$61.5 billion ± $1.5 billion', 'Approximately 85.95%', 'Approximately 86.25%', 'Approximately $2.31 billion', 'Approximately $2.06 billion', '$37.84 ± $1.00', '$38.15 ± $1.00') and bind guidance quote_ids to them. Another: move the quotes out of the table.

findings.title: Guidance code values display with less precision than the adjacent quotes (86.25% shown as 86.2%)
findings.detail: values.json shows guide_gross_margin_next_q_nongaap 0.8625 as '86.2%' (the float rounds down; the conventional result is 86.3%), guide_gross_margin_next_q_gaap 0.8595 as '86.0%', guide_opex_next_q_gaap 2.31e9 as '$2.3bn' and guide_opex_next_q_nongaap 2.06e9 as '$2.1bn'. Next to the verbatim quotes (85.95%, 86.25%, $2.31bn, $2.06bn), the code column looks inconsistent with its source. The stored values themselves are exact.
findings.required_evidence: The note relies on the verbatim quotes for guidance precision (for example, the code column says 'rounded'), or the figures shown match the quoted precision.

findings.title: EPS guidance entries use unit 'USD' instead of the contract unit 'USD/share'
findings.detail: In narrative.json the guidance metrics eps_next_q_gaap (37.84) and eps_next_q_nongaap (38.15) carry unit 'USD'. references/contracts.md requires 'USD/share' for per-share amounts. The displayed values ($37.84 / $38.15) are correct and match Q-4. Only the unit label is off.
findings.required_evidence: Both EPS guidance entries in narrative.json have unit 'USD/share'.

findings.title: Claim that including long-term marketable investments leaves the rating unchanged is unquantified and attributed to a specialist rather than to evidence
findings.detail: The Model and valuation section says that including long-term marketable investments 'would raise the equity value somewhat; according to the valuation specialist, the rating would stay Neutral (not recomputed in code here)'. The snapshot shows long-term marketable investments of $30,019M at 2026-09-03 (periodic.txt line 2032; AvailableForSaleSecuritiesDebtSecuritiesNoncurrent 30,019,000,000 in the 10-K, accn 0000723125-26-000023). That is about 78% of the $38.3bn net cash the note reports, so 'somewhat' understates it. My own arithmetic agrees with the conclusion: both the DCF and the relative method add net cash per share, so adding $30.019bn / 1.145bn shares = +$26.2 per share to both gives a blended value of about $1,110 and upside of about 7.2%. That is still inside the Neutral band. The claim therefore holds, but the note gives no supporting figure. Overlap: the net-cash definition itself belongs to crit-assumption; this finding covers only how the sentence is evidenced.
findings.required_evidence: The sentence either cites the excluded amount through a code value or quote and states the effect as analyst arithmetic, or it is reworded so it makes no unsupported attribution to a specialist.

findings.title: Net cash omits $30.0B of long-term marketable investments
findings.detail: valuation.json gives net_cash = cash 38,364M + short_term_investments 5,070M - debt 5,179M = 38,255M. The 10-K balance sheet (snapshot/docs/periodic.txt, line 2032) also reports 'Long-term marketable investments | 30,019' at 2026-09-03. The release balance sheet (release_ex99_1, line 312) shows the same figure. These are available-for-sale, investment-grade fixed-income securities, mostly maturing in one to five years (periodic.txt lines 2296, 2378, 2416). Management describes them as part of 'Cash and marketable investments totaled $73.45 billion' (periodic.txt line 1761). The item is material: it is about 41% of cash plus investments, almost six times total debt, and about $26 per share on 1,145M diluted shares. My own arithmetic, not code output, adds it to both the DCF and EV/Sales legs: DCF per share goes from about $847 to about $874, relative value from $1,792 to about $1,819, blended target price from $1,084 to about $1,110, and upside from 4.6% to about 7.1%. The rating probably stays Neutral, but the target price and every per-share value are understated. The generator knew about the gap: gen-valuation's report flagged it, and note.md discloses it as 'not recomputed in code here' and cites 'the valuation specialist' for the rating claim. Disclosure does not substitute for the fix, and an uncomputed claim about the rating should not be in the note. A fix needs no code change. The snapshot has AvailableForSaleSecuritiesDebtSecuritiesNoncurrent with 16 observations, latest 30,019M at 2026-09-03 (eu.py concepts --line short_term_investments). contracts.md allows a list of concepts summed per period. Non-marketable equity investments of $1.30B in other noncurrent assets (periodic.txt line 2432) can reasonably stay excluded.
evidence: snapshot/docs/periodic.txt:1761 'Cash and marketable investments totaled $73.45 billion as of September 3, 2026'
findings.required_evidence: mapping.json maps the investments line to [AvailableForSaleSecuritiesDebtSecuritiesCurrent, AvailableForSaleSecuritiesDebtSecuritiesNoncurrent], or equivalent, with a rationale. Recomputed valuation.json then shows investments of 35,089M and net_cash of 68,274M at 2026-09-03. note.md describes net cash as cash and marketable investments less debt and drops the uncomputed 'rating would stay Neutral' claim.

findings.title: Refundable customer deposits ($12.9B) not considered as a debt-like claim
findings.detail: The balance sheet shows 'Noncurrent customer contract liabilities | 12,895' (periodic.txt line 2056; $142M a year earlier). These are mainly customer deposits under the strategic customer agreements, received as a $12.75B financing inflow in FY2026 (line 1842; cash flow line 2228). The deposits are returned if customers meet their purchase commitments, and 'Nearly all of the deposits are scheduled to be repaid between 2029 and 2031' (line 2961). That falls inside DCF years 3-5. Reported cash includes this money, but neither net cash nor the FCF path reflects the repayment. The WACC rationale also calls debt 'small ($5.179B ...)' without mentioning these deposits. The balance sheet does not label them debt, so excluding them is a defensible judgment. The impact is about $11 per share, roughly 1% of the target price. The rationale should acknowledge the exclusion, and the note should mention it as a valuation caveat.
findings.required_evidence: valuation_inputs.json rationale, ideally also the note, states how the $12.9B refundable customer deposits are treated (excluded as operating liabilities, or deducted as debt-like) and why.

findings.title: Year-1 FCF margin rationale ignores the guided capex and working capital
findings.detail: Year-1 FCF margin is 55%, which gives FCF of $148.2B on NTM revenue of $269.5B. The rationale anchors it on history (FY2026 44.3%, FY2026Q4 60.6% in a 14-week quarter) and says capex keeps rising. It does not cite the 10-K's explicit capex outlook: 'approximately $11.5 billion in the first quarter of 2027, approximately $25 billion in the first six months of 2027, and higher in the second half of 2027' (periodic.txt line 1771). My rough check, not code output: NTM net income $188.7B plus D&A of about $10B (FY2026 $9.5B, line 2187) minus capex of at least about $50B gives about $148B, or 55%, only if working capital is zero. Receivables rose from $9.3B to $36.2B in FY2026, so working-capital absorption is likely while revenue grows. FY2026Q4 CFO was also helped by noncurrent Pillar Two taxes payable (line 1832). 55% is at the top of the plausible range. It needs the guided capex in its support, or a small reduction.
findings.required_evidence: The fcf_margin rationale cites the FY2027 capex guidance (as a quote) and reconciles the year-1 margin with NTM net income + D&A - guided capex - working capital, or lowers the year-1 margin accordingly.

findings.title: Data-source disclosure misattributes the earnings release to the 10-K accession and omits the 8-K accession
findings.detail: The Disclosures section (note.md line 74) says: 'SEC EDGAR filing accession 0000723125-26-000023 (Form 10-K and the accompanying earnings release exhibit)'. The earnings release is not an exhibit to the 10-K. snapshot/manifest.json lists docs/release_ex99_1 earnings release.txt as accession 0000723125-26-000018 (document a2026q4ex991-pressrelease.htm), and snapshot/filings.json shows that accession is a Form 8-K (items 2.02, 9.01) accepted 2026-09-30T20:02:22Z. The 10-K (accession ...-000023) was accepted 2026-10-09T12:21:00Z. The guidance table, the CEO quote, the dividend quote and the Q4 EPS guidance all come from the 8-K release, and the note never discloses that source's accession. Policy section 6 requires the data sources with SEC EDGAR filing accession and as-of time. The disclosure is there but inaccurate for a main data source. Timing is fine: the 8-K is before the cutoff, so there is no leakage. Note for repair: values.json has no key for the release accession (only trigger_accession), and the writer may not type digits. A full fix may need a code-provided key such as release_accession. At minimum the writer must remove the false 'accompanying earnings release exhibit' wording and name the release as a separate Form 8-K filed before the 10-K.
findings.required_evidence: note_rendered.md Disclosures names the 10-K (0000723125-26-000023) and the separate Form 8-K earnings release (0000723125-26-000018, furnished 2026-09-30) as data sources, and no longer calls the release an exhibit to the 10-K

findings.title: Guidance table breaks in rendering because quoted cells contain pipe characters
findings.detail: Each verbatim guidance quote (Q-1 to Q-4) contains '| |' from the release's GAAP/non-GAAP table, e.g. '| Revenue | “$61.5 billion ± $1.5 billion | | $61.5 billion ± $1.5 billion” | $61.5bn midpoint |'. In GitHub-flavoured Markdown each row splits into five cells under a three-column header, and the extra cells are dropped. The published table would show only the GAAP half of each quote, with an unclosed quotation mark, and an empty 'Code value used' column. The non-GAAP gross margin, opex and EPS values appear only in this table, so the reader loses them. The figures are correct; this is a presentation defect.
findings.required_evidence: Guidance shown so that it renders correctly, e.g. as a list or with the pipes escaped, while the quotes stay verifiable

findings.title: Rating-robustness claim attributed to 'the valuation specialist' rather than to evidence
findings.detail: note.md line 60: 'Including them would raise the equity value somewhat; according to the valuation specialist, the rating would stay Neutral (not recomputed in code here).' The claim itself holds. RUN_NOTES records long-term marketable investments of $30.019B (AvailableForSaleSecuritiesDebtSecuritiesNoncurrent, F-5368223b24), which is about +$26 per share on 1,145M diluted shares. That gives roughly $1,110 and about 7% upside, still Neutral. But a published note should not cite an internal workflow role as authority. Label the statement as our calculation or judgment, or have code supply the figure.
evidence: RUN_NOTES.md (open question on long-term marketable investments)
findings.required_evidence: Sentence labelled as analyst calculation or judgment (or backed by a code value), with no reference to an internal specialist
